frozen_candidate_root_contribution: ywm denotes a bounded/delimited stretch of time held as a single reckoned unit or occasion -- countable, sequenceable, and individuatable either by calendar position or by the event that fills it. Its magnitude (a solar day, a creative epoch, 1,000 or 50,000 years) and its content (judgment, battle, festival, fast, weekday, salvation) are supplied entirely by context/qualifier and are NOT fixed by the root. Number morphology counts such periods (sg 1 / du 2 / pl several).

internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 405 occurrences the root ywm names 'a day' in the sense of a bounded span of time treated as one countable occasion, without fixing how long it is or what happens in it. The famous eschatological uses -- yawm al-qiyamah, yawm al-din, al-yawm al-akhir, and the adverbial 'yawma [judgment scene]' clauses -- get their finality from the annexed word or clause, not from ywm itself: the identical grammar 'yawm + defining term' also yields Friday (62:9), Badr / the day the two hosts met (8:41), Moses' festival day (20:59), and the six creation-days. The text even measures 'a day' at 1,000 and 50,000 years (32:5, 70:4, 22:47), proving the length is context-set. The N vs T tag is only syntax (governed noun vs adverb-of-time), not a change of meaning; singular/dual/plural just count the periods. A productive metonymy (period -> the event/fate that fills it) generates the figurative plural 'ayyam Allah' and 'tilka l-ayyam nudawiluha', which strain but do not break the single nucleus.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: ywm does NOT entail: (1) a fixed duration / '24-hour solar day' -- disproved by 32:5, 70:4, 22:47 (miqdar = 1,000 / 50,000 years) and the phased creation of 41:9-12 (2+4+2 days); (2) 'daylight vs night' -- that contrast is carried by nahar/layl, and ywm pairs WITH layali as full units (69:7, 34:18); (3) a durationless instant/point -- that is sa'ah, explicitly the finer sub-unit contrasted with yawm at 30:55; (4) judgment/resurrection in itself -- strip the annex (al-qiyamah/al-din/al-fasl or the verbal clause) and ywm is neutral (worldly yawm al-hajj al-akbar 9:3); (5) a self-standing proper name -- it needs an article/deixis or annexed specifier to fix a referent; (6) anything non-temporal -- no occurrence denotes a place, object, or person.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 70:4:6:1 (fi yawmin kana miqdaruhu khamsina alfa sanatin) predicates miqdar (measure) of fifty thousand years on a single yawm, and 32:5:11:1 gives 'alfa sanatin mimma ta'uddun' (a thousand of the years you count) while 22:47:8:1 gives 'ka-alfi sanatin mimma ta'uddun' -- the SAME year-currency (sanah) used to count ordinary days. The Quran thus measures even the cosmic Day in the currency of counted days, giving two different magnitudes (1,000 vs 50,000 years) for 'a yawm'. This is the strongest counterexample to the tempting narrow gloss 'solar / 24-hour day': it kills that reading while positively confirming the scale-neutral nucleus (ywm = a bounded reckoned span whose magnitude is fixed by context, not by the root).
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: Two-class / homonymy account: split ywm into (1) an ordinary calendrical day (pluralisable as ayyam/yawmayn: six creation-days, fasting-days, Friday, Badr) and (2) a lexicalised theological term 'the Day' (Judgment) -- unique, never pluralised, always singular / definite / annexed, carrying fixed eschatological content -- on the ground that 24 hours vs 50,000 years are too disparate to be one concept. This is REJECTED Quran-internally: (a) al-yawma slides between worldly 'today' (12:92, 19:26, 10:92) and eschatological 'today' (40:17, 45:34) with zero morphological difference; (b) the construction 'yawm + defining genitive' is one productive pattern yielding both worldly yawm al-hajj al-akbar (9:3) and yawm al-din (1:4); (c) the great Day is itself reckoned as a span measured in years (70:4) and quantified as a day-unit ('yawman mina l-'adhab' 40:49), tying it to the very reckoned-span nucleus shared with the six creation-ayyam. The two-class account over-generates: one nucleus + context + reference explains all 405. The uniqueness / non-pluralisation of the eschatological Day follows from REFERENCE (there is one final Day) and definite/annexed syntax, not from a separate root sense.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three independent lenses (two constructive, one adversarial) converge, from opposite directions, on a single scale-neutral, event-neutral nucleus and find NO Quran-internal occurrence that is non-temporal or that forces two unbridged classes. Morphology is uniform (qac_verb_form null throughout; only nominal N=325 / adverbial-of-time T=80, which share the identical referential range, e.g. the same surface 'yawma' is tagged N 150x and T 78x). The number bridge is demonstrated internally: dual yawmayn (41:9, 41:12) + plural 'six ayyam' reconcile as one counting system (2+2+... of creation), and the plural is used for literal counted spans (fasting 2:184, hajj 2:203). The nucleus is positively DEMANDED, not merely permitted, by the miqdar-in-years verses (32:5/70:4/22:47) and by the deictic continuity of al-yawma across worldly and eschatological registers. It is sharply distinguished from semantic neighbours -- sa'ah (point/instant, 30:55), nahar/layl (light-phase), sana/ajal (fixed length / appointed deadline) -- so the account is a genuine narrowest altitude, not a fit-everything abstraction. The dominant eschatological collocation is a frequent CONTEXTUAL specialisation (high frequency != root meaning; same gloss != synonymy), refuted as a root sense by the non-eschatological occurrences (creation epochs, Friday, Badr, festival, the year-measures) that independently converge on the same core. Result is STRONG but not universally established because a productive metonymic ayyam cluster (3:140, ayyam Allah 14:5/45:14, 10:102, 69:24) shows the sense is productive rather than fixed -- recorded as resistant seams, bridged not broken.

reconciliation.rationale: All three lenses independently flag it as the single most resistant occurrence: the contentful meaning (alternated fortunes) sits in the verb nudawil and ywm supplies only period-as-vehicle. Honesty over forced unity -> marked RESISTANT, but bridged (metonymy period->its fate), so it does not license an unbridged class.
ayyam here means God's decisive interventions/epochs, not counted calendar days; the same period->event metonymy as 3:140. Marked RESISTANT_SEAM, bridged.

adversarial_verification.notes: The adversarial lens (C) actively sought a Quran-internal disproof and could produce none that denotes anything non-temporal or forces two unbridged classes; the only account that would split ywm (24h day vs cosmic epoch) is explicitly refuted by the root's own miqdar-in-years predication (32:5/70:4/22:47). The nucleus is distinct from sa'ah, nahar/layl, and sana/ajal. Status is NOT_RUN (not PASSED) because genuine resistant seams persist -- the productive metonymic ayyam cluster (3:140, 14:5, 45:14, 10:102, 69:24) strains the nucleus (the root does least work there); the core holds and these are recorded as RESISTANT_SEAM hard cases + counterevidence rather than treated as clean failures.

layer_attribution.derivation: No verbal derivation in the corpus (qac_verb_form null for all 405). The root surfaces only as a noun; the sole morphological axes are grammatical number (sg/du/pl) and the syntactic N (governed noun) vs T (adverb-of-time) government, neither of which carries meaning -- the same surface 'yawma' is tagged N 150x and T 78x.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: Single lexical class: a countable time-noun. The unique eschatological 'Day' (yawm al-qiyamah / al-yawm al-akhir / yawm al-din) is a REFERENTIAL specialisation fixed by definite/annexed syntax and by there being one final Day -- not a second lexeme; it never pluralises for that reason, whereas ayyam serves multiple/ordinary/notable days.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Magnitude and content are contributed by the annexed term or clause ('yawm + defining event': al-din, al-qiyamah, al-fasl, al-hajj al-akbar, iltaqa l-jam'an, al-zinah) or by article/deixis (al-yawma). The judgment/finality is contextual, NOT root content -- strip the qualifier and ywm reverts to a neutral bounded period (62:9 Friday, 3:140 worldly turns, six creation-days).
layer_attribution.reconciliation: The dual/plural counting reconciles with the singular via one internal counting system (41:9 + 41:12 yawmayn+yawmayn vs 'six ayyam' of creation; fasting/hajj counts). Deictic al-yawma bridges worldly (12:92) and eschatological (40:17) registers with zero morphological difference. N and T reconcile as one sense under two governments.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: A productive metonymic ayyam cluster (3:140, 14:5, 45:14, 10:102, 69:24: period -> its defining event/fate) strains the plain reckoned-period reading and is retained as RESISTANT_SEAM (bridged, not an unbridged class). One genuinely UNRESOLVED micro-question: whether ywm ever narrows to the daylight-half in the layl+yawm pairings (69:7, 34:18) -- evidence compatible but non-decisive.

hard_cases.reason: The 50,000-year yawm (with 32:5, 22:47) is the sharpest blade against unity: naively it would split ywm into calendrical-day vs cosmic-epoch. But the same verses predicate miqdar-in-years marked 'mimma ta'uddun', commensurating the great Day with counted days, so it kills only the over-narrow '24-hour day' gloss and confirms the scale-neutral nucleus.

evidence_basis.statement: 70:4:6:1 (fi yawmin kana miqdaruhu khamsina alfa sanatin) predicates miqdar (measure) of fifty thousand years on a single yawm, and 32:5:11:1 gives 'alfa sanatin mimma ta'uddun' (a thousand of the years you count) while 22:47:8:1 gives 'ka-alfi sanatin mimma ta'uddun' -- the SAME year-currency (sanah) used to count ordinary days. The Quran thus measures even the cosmic Day in the currency of counted days, giving two different magnitudes (1,000 vs 50,000 years) for 'a yawm'. This is the strongest counterexample to the tempting narrow gloss 'solar / 24-hour day': it kills that reading while positively confirming the scale-neutral nucleus (ywm = a bounded reckoned span whose magnitude is fixed by context, not by the root).

hard_cases.reason: Most resistant occurrence per all three lenses: 'tilka l-ayyamu nudawiluha' -- ywm does the least work, meaning drifts to alternated fortunes/vicissitudes via the period->event metonymy.

evidence_basis.statement: 3:140:10:2 'wa-tilka l-ayyamu nudawiluha bayna l-nas' -- the contentful sense (alternated fortunes / turns of victory and defeat) is carried by the verb nudawil; ywm here contributes only the thinnest residue, period-as-vehicle. This is the case where the root does the least work; it is reached by the productive metonymy period -> what characterises the period, so it strains but does not fracture the nucleus into an unbridged class. Recorded as RESISTANT_SEAM, not a unity-breaker.

hard_cases.reason: ayyam Allah = God's decisive epochs/interventions, not counted days.

evidence_basis.statement: 14:5:13:2 'dhakkirhum bi-ayyami-llah' (the Days of Allah) -- 'ayyam' = God's decisive historical interventions/epochs, not counted calendar days; reached by the metonymy period -> its defining event. Strains the plain 'reckoned period' reading but stays temporal and bridged to the nucleus. RESISTANT_SEAM.

hard_cases.reason: ayyam Allah (they hope not for the Days of Allah) = momentous divine occasions.

evidence_basis.statement: 45:14:8:1 'la yarjuna ayyama-llah' (they do not hope for the Days of Allah) -- same ayyam-Allah metonymy as 14:5: momentous divine occasions, not calendar days. RESISTANT_SEAM, bridged via period -> defining event.

hard_cases.reason: 'ayyam alladhina khalaw' = the fateful befallings of former peoples.

evidence_basis.statement: 10:102:5:1 'mithla ayyami lladhina khalaw min qablihim' -- the fateful days/befallings of former peoples, i.e. the events that filled those periods rather than counted days. Metonymy period -> its fate; strains but does not break the nucleus. RESISTANT_SEAM.

hard_cases.reason: 'al-ayyam al-khaliyah' drifts toward the lived period and its deeds.

evidence_basis.statement: 69:24:7:2 'bima aslaftum fi l-ayyami l-khaliyah' (what you sent ahead in the bygone days) -- ayyam drifts toward the lived period/its deeds; the thinnest 'counted day' residue. Bridged by the same metonymy, RESISTANT_SEAM.

hard_case_representation.rationale: Genuine hard cases exist and are evidence-derived from the packet: one adversarial boundary (the miqdar-in-years verses that kill the '24-hour day' gloss while confirming scale-neutrality) and a productive metonymic ayyam cluster (period -> its defining event/fate) that strains but does not fracture the single nucleus. Each hard case's evidence_basis.statement is persisted verbatim in strongest_counterexample (70:4) or in the corresponding occurrence_override note (the RESISTANT_SEAM refs).

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quran-internal occurrence in which ywm/ayyam/yawmayn denotes something the scale-neutral nucleus excludes -- e.g. a non-temporal referent (place, object, person), a durationless instant proper to sa'ah, or the daylight-half in opposition to layl -- OR a pair of senses with NO Quran-internal bridge, which would refute the claim that ywm carries a single UNIVERSAL, root-wide, scale-neutral bounded period/occasion nucleus and force a multi-class result.
rejection_condition.search_location: The layl+yawm/ayyam pairings 69:7:6:1 (sab'a layalin wa-thamaniyata ayyam) and 34:18:16:2 (layaliya wa-ayyaman) for a forced daylight-half reading; the distributive 55:29:7:1 (kulla yawmin huwa fi sha'n) for a 'continually/every-moment' reading that would dissolve the bounded-unit sense; and the eschatological singular Day vs the counted plural ayyam for any bridge failure.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Re-read each candidate verse_text in the packet and test whether the bounded-reckoned-period reading is merely compatible or is actually FORCED out; check whether nahar/layl or sa'ah, not ywm, carries the contested contrast; confirm dual/plural counting reconciles with the singular via the creation-days system (41:9-12 vs 'six days').
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Attribute finality/judgment to the annexed genitive or verbal clause (al-qiyamah, al-din, al-fasl, iltaqa l-jam'an), not to ywm; strip the qualifier before assigning meaning; do not let dominant eschatological frequency (high frequency != truth) or a shared gloss (same gloss != synonymy) be counted as root content; hold N/T as syntax, not sense.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If such an occurrence is confirmed, demote from UNIVERSAL/ROOT_GENERALIZATION to REPRESENTATIVE (LEXICALIZED_CLASS for the eschatological Day) or to LOCAL/UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY, move the offending refs to counterevidence, and reopen the falsification.

reopen_conditions: If the layl+yawm pairings 69:7:6:1 and 34:18:16:2 are shown to FORCE a 'daylight-half' reading of ywm (rather than merely permit it), splitting ywm from the whole-day-unit nucleus -- currently left as the one minor UNRESOLVED micro-question.

If the metonymic ayyam cluster (3:140:10:2 nudawiluha, 14:5:13:2 / 45:14:8:1 ayyam Allah, 10:102:5:1 ayyam alladhina khalaw, 69:24:7:2 al-ayyam al-khaliyah) is judged to constitute a distinct lexicalised 'notable epochs/vicissitudes' sense with NO bridge to the counted-period core -- which would move these from RESISTANT_SEAM to an unbridged class.

If the miqdar-in-years verses (32:5:11:1, 70:4:6:1, 22:47:8:1) are re-read as evidence that the eschatological/cosmic Day is a SEPARATE lexeme from the calendrical day rather than the same reckoned-span kind at larger scale, reviving the two-class competitor.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The adversarial lens (C) actively sought a Quran-internal disproof and could produce none that denotes anything non-temporal or forces two unbridged classes; the only account that would split ywm (24h day vs cosmic epoch) is explicitly refuted by the root's own miqdar-in-years predication (32:5/70:4/22:47). The nucleus is distinct from sa'ah, nahar/layl, and sana/ajal. Status is NOT_RUN (not PASSED) because genuine resistant seams persist -- the productive metonymic ayyam cluster (3:140, 14:5, 45:14, 10:102, 69:24) strains the nucleus (the root does least work there); the core holds and these are recorded as RESISTANT_SEAM hard cases + counterevidence rather than treated as clean failures.
